display_name: Judge both edges of a gauge canary
description: GAU-15 item 4 (2026-08-19). Judges whether a gauge canary proves the staleness detector works, on BOTH edges: it alarmed when tampered, and it stayed quiet when healthy. The two edges are read from independent evidence and are not each other's complement -- a canary that never alarms passes the quiet edge and fails the armed one, and a canary that alarms constantly does the reverse, which is exactly why one edge alone is not a test. Alarms are attributed by time AND type: an alarm falling inside a logged arrest window whose expected type it matches is SCHEDULED, and everything else is UNATTRIBUTED. Requiring the type to match as well as the time is what stops a genuine coverage fault that happened to land during a staleness arrest from being quietly absorbed as the alarm that was asked for, which would turn a real finding into a pass. Only CLOSED windows are judged; a window still open has not had its chance, and counting it as a missing alarm would fail the canary for being asked too early. The verdict is built from the durable notice record rather than the in-memory bridge event queue, and that is a correctness requirement rather than a preference: the queue's only reader REMOVES what it reads, so a verifier polling it would race the steward and could consume the very alarm the steward needed. Finally, deployment capability is an input rather than an assumption: expecting an alarm from a release whose sweep carries no staleness detector is a test that fails for the wrong reason, so when the detector's presence in the running release is not established the verdict is ABSTAINED. A verdict about an instrument that is not running is a false accusation whichever way it lands. A PASS requires POSITIVE EVIDENCE: at least one CLOSED arrest window that produced the alarm it asked for. A run in which nothing was exercised -- no closed window, no alarm -- returns the distinct verdict 'no_evidence' and never a pass, because silence is exactly what an unexercised canary and a detector that can no longer fire have in common, and the quiet edge alone therefore cannot justify a pass. This is the defect the verifier itself carried until 2026-08-19, when a zero-window run returned 'both edges hold' -- a vacuous green inside the instrument built to detect vacuous greens. Standing convention, fleet-wide: quote every verdict together with its closed-window count, and read a zero-window result as untested.
embedding_description: Checking whether a deliberately broken fake session actually triggered the alarm it was supposed to, and whether any unexpected alarms fired, to establish that the monitoring both catches faults and stays quiet otherwise.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: verdict (pass | fail | abstained | no_evidence), verdict_reason, agent_instance_id, detector_deployed, windows_examined, closed_windows, windows_with_expected_alarm, silent_windows, alarms_examined, scheduled_alarms, unattributed_alarms, truncated, since.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with the verdict AND its closed-window count -- never the verdict alone, because a green that exercised nothing reads identically to one that was earned. Treat 'no_evidence' as UNTESTED: the canary was never exercised in this range, which is neither a passing instrument nor a failing one, and reporting it as a pass is the specific error this verdict exists to prevent. Treat 'abstained' as a statement about deployment, NOT as a soft failure of the detector -- say the detector was not established as running and stop there. When silent_windows is greater than zero, that is the armed edge failing and is the more serious finding. When unattributed_alarms is greater than zero, do NOT describe them as canary noise: they are either a real fault or a gap in the audit log, and both need a reader.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: A pass proves the instrument CAN catch. It is NOT a live catch and must never be recorded as one -- catching a real freeze in production is a separate evidence class that stays open regardless of how many canary passes accumulate.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Two bounded ordered reads -- the canary's tamper windows and its durable gauge-notice records -- through the state interface. Read-only.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound. A canary with no windows and no alarms is NOT an error -- it returns a normal successful result whose verdict is 'no_evidence'. Both 'abstained' and 'no_evidence' are verdicts, not errors.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: If the verdict is abstained, establish whether the running release actually carries the staleness detector (the release capability probe answers this) and pass detector_deployed explicitly. If the verdict is no_evidence, nothing was exercised: arrest the canary through the audited tamper verb, wait for the window to CLOSE, and verify again -- an open window has not had its chance yet. If a window you expected is missing, widen the range with since before concluding the arrest never happened.
